reason: Reviewed all five surfaces for guided setup across the CLI and the skill. CLI readiness: `init --json` returns a first `apps` gap (question message, technical.supported and technical.detected) when no agent app is connected and neither --apps nor the older per-piece flags were given; the answer, none included, is remembered in the state directory so the gap never returns; --apps installs hooks, the skill (global unless --skills-scope project, never asked) and Claude Code/Codex command approval without asking, and command approval also covers `notifai init` so reruns do not prompt. --wait (only with --json; otherwise a usage error) keeps a run watching the User’s step and adds top-level message (only when new for the setup run), waiting and stopped. The approval page and the already-connected phone page open in the browser except over SSH, with --no-open or with --approval notification; approval codes last 30 minutes and are extended with the same code while setup waits; an unextendable code is replaced ("That code expired. New one: …", named once); the 90-minute stop counts from when the approval began, kept with the saved handshake, and says "Tell me when you want to try again."; stop ("almost there") messages promise no test notification. After a browser approval setup opened, the phone message is "Now your phone: follow the page in your browser." with no store QR; the /setup/phone link, built by the protocol, carries the computer name for display. The test notification goes out at most once per computer and phone: the CLI asks GET /api/v1/machine/setup-notification and sends nothing when the browser or an earlier run already did, and retries a refused send once after the phone’s last_seen_at moves on. A terminal whose Companion App only waits on the plan moves on to the plan step; a terminal setup whose phone has notifications off ends with the same done content as --json. During init the hooks-trust state is an optional gap whose message is the done message’s short Codex /hooks warning; outside setup (doctor, a refused ask) the codex_hook_approval_required message names the same CODEX_HOME and turning the hooks on. Device nouns come from one helper (Android is "Android phone"). Notifai skill and harness setup: setup guidance runs one loop, notifai init --json --wait 240: send message whenever present (including with waiting: true), rerun at once on waiting, end the turn on stopped and finish on done, so agents never ask the User to report a step; the only question is which agent apps to connect, asked once from the apps gap and passed as --apps; the Claude Code and Codex command-approval sections and the Hermes skill line say command approval and the machine-wide skill come with the chosen apps. The approve-link, choices, claude-session and done-no-questions scripts are removed because setup’s own messages carry the code, link and per-app next steps; install, cloud, which-computer and installer-needs-you are shortened, and a done script remains for an older CLI, which is updated with notifai update or falls back to the earlier non-waiting loop. The QR stays in the conversation and never in a Notification Request. Domain terms: "Setup notification" and "Phone sign-in" name these concepts; User-facing copy keeps "test notification". Lifecycle hooks are unchanged. USAGE.md describes the new flow. Exact session naming review: native T3 mappings and explicit Codex names enrich generated fallbacks during attendance without changing these setup instructions, activation or question routing. The skill still requires session-label on sends and asks and explicit rename only for a changed job. Automatic enrichment preserves semantic labels and User renames; old services keep baseline sends and attendance. Local content-free diagnostics identify name-resolution outcomes and sends by Agent Session. Reviewed the additive registration, upload-grant and support-assessment schemas against lifecycle hooks, the Notifai skill, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms. Existing response fields and optional support metadata retain their types; new exported validators do not change CLI call sites, which continue to use the response types. These protocol additions introduce no command, setup action, readiness state, lifecycle behavior or domain term requiring agent guidance changes. Reviewed access and changes-feed response schemas against lifecycle hooks, the Notifai skill, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms. CLI accessStatus retains its existing call path and wire fields; the new exported guards are not invoked by CLI commands or harness integrations. Required feed row schemas preserve optional metadata and additive fields, and do not change attendance, readiness, session lifecycle or user instructions. Nested historical content remains explicitly outside deep response validation. No agent guidance text changes are needed. Reviewed the retained draft, reply, acknowledgement and answer schemas against lifecycle hooks, the Notifai skill, harness setup, CLI readiness and domain terms. The CLI uses the unchanged reply and answer structures as types; no CLI command or hook invokes these feed decoders. Output schemas preserve optional metadata and additive fields, and do not alter submission validators, attendance, readiness or instruction text. Deep validation of retained feed content needs no agent guidance changes.
